- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); for first 3–5 forecast days, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.2–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of past 30d to anchor forecast mid-range.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model overestimates upward trends when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent 14d high to avoid inflationary bias.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment misalignment.
